3  O.S. No.2353/2013  JUDGMENT Suit is one for Partition and Separate Possession of plaintiffs  share in the suit property and for declaration that registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003 is not binding on the plaintiffs.

2. Case of the plaintiffs in brief is as hereunder:-
One Muniyappa was the original propositus of the family of the plaintiffs and defendants and he had four sons namely Achappa, Narayanappa, Ramakrishnappa and Munishamappa.
The plaintiffs are the children of Late.
Narayanappa and defendant No.1 is the son of Late.
Achappa and the defendant No.2 is the son of Ramakrishnappa and Munishamappa died issue less.
It is stated that the suit properties are the ancestral and joint family properties of plaintiffs and defendants and they constitute an Hindu Undivided Joint Family.

After the death of the propositus Muniyappa, his son Achappa O.S. No.2353/2013 looked after the welfare of the joint family and after his demise the defendant No.1 looked after the affairs of the joint family and as such, he became the kartha of the joint family constituted by the plaintiffs and the defendants.
Hence, the suit properties are standing in the name of defendant No.1.

The plaintiffs and the defendants being in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit properties have acquired right, title and interest and due to enlargement of the joint family, they are residing separately, but no partition is Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
2 effected between the family members.
After the demise of Achappa, the defendants No.1 and 2 started acting adverse to the interest of the joint family and hence, the plaintiffs demanded to effect partition of the suit properties.
The defendants though initially agreed, later they postponed the same on one or the other pretext.
Later the defendants without the consent or knowledge of the plaintiffs have partitioned the suit properties under O.S. No.2353/2013 registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003.
Based on the partition deed mutation is also the effected in the name of defendants No.1 and 2.
Since the alleged partition is made without the consent or knowledge of the plaintiffs, the same is not binding upon them.

3. It is further stated that the land bearing Sy. No.147/1 measuring 1 acre 36 guntas was acquired by K.I.A.D.B and compensation of Rs.26,29,261/- was awarded and the plaintiffs are also entitled for share in the compensation amount.

Since the defendants started acting adverse to the interest of the plaintiffs and refused to allot their legitimate share and got executed registered partition deed without the knowledge of the plaintiffs, the present suit is filed.

4. Inspite of due service of summons, the defendant No.2 remained absent and hence is placed O.S.
No.2353/2013 exparte.

In pursuance to the summons issued, the defendant No.1 caused appearance and filed written statement, wherein which he has admitted the relationship, but has categorically denied all the other allegations made in the plaint.
It is stated that the plaintiffs have deliberately suppressed the registered transactions and judicial proceedings in respect of the properties over last 60 to 70 years.

The suppression of the registered transactions and judicial proceedings demonstrate that the plaintiffs can have no claim over the suit properties and the defendant's family is in absolute possession and enjoyment of the properties allotted to this defendant No.1 and there is no cause of action to file the suit and the claim of the plaintiff is barred by the provisions of limitation and hence, the suit is not maintainable.

It is contended that the propositus Sri. Muniyappa died prior to 1940 and thereafter, this defendant's father Late. Achappa was managing the O.S. No.2353/2013 properties owned by the family with the consent of his brother including Late. Narayanappa.
The said Achappa and his brothers mortgaged the properties under three mortgage deed dated 21.02.1947, 12.07.1947 and 04.06.1952 in favour of one Sri. D.V.Irachan.
The father of the plaintiffs Sri. Narayanappa executed sale deed in favour of Achappa on 04.06.1952 transferring his undivided share in the suit property.

The first and second mortgage deeds were executed by the Achappa and his two brothers Ramakrishna and Munishamappa and the third mortgage deed was executed to purchase Narayanappa's share and on the same day sale deed was executed by Narayanappa in favour of Achappa.

These transactions and the subsequent transactions establish that Narayanappa did not have any share in the suit properties with the execution of the sale deed conveying his right in favour of Late. Achappa.

Later, the Achappa and his two brothers transferred the properties in favour of Ramaiah S/o.
Chatra Subbaiah under sale deed dated 23.05.1956 to discharge the amounts due under the mortgage deeds and later, Achappa and Ramakrishnappa repurchased the properties from Ramaiah under sale deed dated 11.07.1960.

Subsequently, Ramakrishnappa transferred his share in favour of Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
3 Achappa under sale deed dated 17.09.1962 and thus after the demise of last brother Munishamappa,
Late. Achappa and this defendant were entitled to equal share in these properties and none of the the other family members had any right over the same.

It is further stated that this defendant No.1 filed a suit against his father Achappa in O.S. No.794/1980 seeking partition and the suit came to be decreed on 13.02.1987 and the judgment was affirmed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.4151/1987 dated 09.10.1987.

Later, this defendant initiated final O.S. No.2353/2013 decree proceedings in F.D.P. No.10009/1988 and this defendant was put in possession of his share in item No.1 to 3 and this defendant is the absolute owner of the shares allotted to him.

6. It is further stated that Late. Achappa despite of the judgment and decree passed in O.S.
No.784/1980 and R.F.A. No.415//1987 executed a registered Will in favour of defendant No.2 and the suit filed by defendant No.2 also came to be dismissed and thereafter, the defendant No.2 along with his mother Smt. Rathnamma entered into partition deed dated 17.12.2003.

By virtue of the said partition, the defendant No.2 and his mother affirmed the title of this defendant No.1 to the properties allotted to him, while this defendant affirmed the title of defendant No.2 to Achappa's share as a legatee under the Will executed by him and in consideration thereof a small portion of the property from Achappa's share in Sy.
O.S. No.2353/2013 No.162 and 160/1 measuring 60X40 ft. was allotted to defendant No.1 and accordingly, the khata is effected to the name of defendant No.1.

The plaintiffs being aware of all these transactions have filed the suit by suppressing material facts and since certain portion of properties in Sy. No.160/1 and 162 was acquired by the Karnataka Slum Clearance Board, shares are allotted under the partition deed excluding such extent of acquired land and these lands have also lost the status of agricultural lands.

It is denied that Sy. No.147/1 was acquired by K.I.A.D.B and it is stated that a portion of the land Sy. No.147/1 was acquired by the defense and the other portion was later notified for acquisition for the benefit the defense department way back in the year1960-70.

The compensation payable was subject matter in L.A.C. No.598/1919 which was contested by Late.
Achappa and this defendant and this defendant has received compensation in terms of the order passed O.S. No.2353/2013 by the competent Court including the judgment passed in O.S.
No.794/2018 and R.F.A. No.415/1987 and hence, the suit is barred by law of limitation and the plaintiffs are not entitled for the reliefs claimed and sought for dismissal of suit.
7. The aforesaid pleadings have occasioned following ;
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiffs prove that the suit schedule properties are ancestral joint family properties of plaintiffs and defendants and they are in joint possession and enjoyment of the same ?
2. Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are entitled for  share in the suit schedule properties ?
3. Whether the plaintiffs further prove that the alleged Partition Deed dated 17.02.2003 is not binding on them ?

8. The plaintiff No.2 in order to establish his claim got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21.
On the Contrary, the defendant No.1 got examined as D.W.1 and relied upon 24 documents marked at Ex.D.1 & Ex.D.24 and closed the evidence.

9. Heard learned counsel for the plaintiffs and defendant and perused records.
10.

The present suit is one for partition and separate possession of plaintiffs  share together in the suit schedule properties and for declaration that the registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003 is not binding upon the plaintiffs.
In the instant case, the relationship between the parties is not in dispute.

One Muniyappa and his wife Chowdamma are the original propositus of the family of the plaintiffs and the defendants and he had O.S. No.2353/2013 4 sons by name Achappa,
Narayanappa, Ramakrishnappa and Munishamappa.
The 1st son Achappa died leaving behind his son i.e. defendant No.1 as his legal heir.
The second son Narayanappa died leaving behind his two sons by name Muniraju and Venkatesh i.e. plaintiff No. 2 herein and Muniraju died leaving behind his wife i.e. plaintiff No.1.
Likewise, the 3 rd son Ramakrishnappa died leaving behind defendant No.2 as his son and the 4th son Munishamappa died unmarried.

According to the plaintiffs, the suit schedule properties are the ancestral and joint family properties and after the demise of Muniyappa,
the Achappa being the eldest member of the family looked after the family affairs as khartha of the joint family and as such, the suit schedule properties stood in his name.

But the plaintiffs and defendants are in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties and they have acquired legitimate right over the same and since their rights over O.S. No.2353/2013 the suit schedule properties were denied by the defendants, the present suit is filed.

12. On the contrary it is the contention of defendant No.1 that the Narayanappa has sold his undivided share in favour of his father Achappa under registered Sale Deed dated 04.06.1952 and Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
5

the other son Ramakrishnappa also transferred his undivided share in favour of Achappa and hence,
there exists no joint family among the family members and the defendants No.1 and 2 by entering into partition deed have partitioned the property which belonged to Achappa and hence, the plaintiffs are not entitled for any share.
13. Before dealing with the merits of the case, it is found necessary to take note of the previous litigations that took place between the parties which are not disputed by either of the parties.

It is not in dispute that, the property bearing Sy. No.147/1 measuring 1 acre 36 O.S. No.2353/2013 guntas was acquired by the K.I.A.D.B. for public purpose and compensation was awarded and thereafter, the matter was referred under Sections 30 and 31 of Land Acquisition Act for enhancement of compensation before the civil Court.
Ex. P.17
to Ex.P.20

which are the copies of judgment and award and order sheet in L.A.C. No.508/1980 and the order sheet in Execution No.1185/2004 shows that the defendants No.1 and 2 along with Rathnamma who is the wife of Ramakrishnappa and also Narayanappa who is the father of plaintiff No.2 and mother Chowdamma i.e. all the family members filed this reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act seeking enhancement of the compensation amount and the Court vide judgment dated 26.07.2003 has accepted the reference and the compensation amount is enhanced.

It is also seen from the records that during the pendency of this petition Achappa died leaving behind his wife Lakshmamma and O.S. No.2353/2013 his son i.e. the defendant No.1 herein and they were brought on record and likewise, the other son Ramakrishnappa also died and his wife and children were brought on record.

The observation made in the order shows that Rathnamma, Narayanappa and Chowdamma have not claimed any share over any extent in the acquire lands and hence, the legal heir of Achappa is held entitled for 50% of compensation amount and likewise the legal heirs of Ramakrishnappa are together entitled for 50% of the compensation amount and no share is allotted to the father of the plaintiffs Narayanappa and Chowdamma wife of Muniyappa.
So these observations in the order passed by the Court, goes without saying that Narayanappa left the reference uncontested.
Pursuant to the award passed, execution petition was filed by the defendant No.1 herein for recovery of the compensation amount against the concerned authority.

The documents placed on record also shows that during the lifetime of Achappa there arose differences between the Achappa and his son i.e. defendant No.1 herein and hence, defendant No.1 filed suit bearing O.S. No.794/1980 on the file of XI Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru seeking relief of partition and separate possession of his 1 share in the suit schedule properties.

The copy of the judgment placed on record shows that the Achappa had seriously contested the suit and according to the plaintiff therein the suit schedule properties were the joint family and ancestral properties and as such claimed share over the same.

However, Achappa contested the suit and raised a defense that the suit schedule properties are the joint family properties of himself and his other two brothers Narayanappa and Ramakrishnappa and there was no partition among them and any documents executed by their brothers were O.S. No.2353/2013 nominal and were not intended to be acted upon and there was no income from any of these properties and the suit properties were his self acquisitions acquired out of his separate income and had sought for dismissal of suit.

However, the Court held that the Achappa failed to prove his Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
6 separate income to purchase the share of his brothers in the schedule items and therefore, the suit schedule lands were considered to be ancestral and joint family properties of the plaintiff and defendant No.1 therein and hence, the suit was decreed and the defendant No.1 herein was held entitled for  share in the suit schedule items No.1 to 5 and he was also held entitled for compensation amount pertaining to the acquisition of item No.4 of the schedule land.

15. As against the judgment and decree, the father Achappa preferred RFA. No.415/1987 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka vide judgment dated 09.10.1987 O.S. No.2353/2013 dismissed the appeal and the observation of the Hon'ble High Court reads thus:
"On the other hand Ex.D.2, the registered Sale Deed would go to show that the reconveyance of the suit schedule properties took place in favour of Achappa and his brother Ramakrishnappa.

Therefore, on the date of Ex.D.2 they were joint family properties and could not have been purchased by defendant No.1 only and as is evident from the recitals it was no more than that they had themselves sold to Ramaiah.

That coupled with the evidence of D.W.1 as evidenced by Ex.D.1 Shara that the suit schedule properties were inam lands of the ancestral property of the parties and were registered in the name of defendant No.1 on his application under the provision of the Mysuru Personal Inams Abolition Act.
That itself constitutes more than proof that the suit lands were in fact ancestral and not self-acquired.

Therefore,
find no substance in this appeal.
Hence, this appeal stands rejected".
The defendant No.1 herein initiated final decree proceedings as per Ex.D.4 in FDP.
No.10009/1988 and final decree proceedings is drawn and share is allotted to the defendant No.1 herein pertaining to the suit schedule properties involved in the present suit.
So the Hon'ble High Court has held that the suit properties therein where the ancestral and joint family properties constituted by the defendant No.1 and his father Achappa.
None of the other family were parties to the said suit.

17. So now the question that needs to be adjudicated by this Court is as to whether there exists joint family status among the plaintiffs and the defendants and the suit properties are their joint family properties and also as to whether the partition deed effected into between the defendants No.1 and 2 are not binding on the plaintiffs and likewise it is also necessary O.S. No.2353/2013 to consider as to whether the ancestor of plaintiffs has alienated his share in favour of the father of defendant No.1 in his capacity as a kartha of the family for the purpose of their legal and family necessity.
18.
It is well settled proposition of law that there is always presumption as to the existence of joint family status between the parties.
In Hindu law, a joint family is presumed to exist among Hindu coparceners and they are presumed to be members of a pint family.
However the presumption can be rebutted by showing that the family has been severed.

But in the instant case, since the plaintiffs are challenging the partition deed, the initial burden is upon them to prove the existence of joint Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
7 family status.

19. The plaintiffs in order to discharge the initial burden cast upon them got examined the plaintiff No.2 as P.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that the O.S. No.2353/2013 suit schedule properties are the ancestral and joint family properties of the plaintiffs and defendants.

After the demise of Muniyappa the father of defendant No.1 Achappa looked after the welfare of the joint family as kartha and as such, all the documents pertaining to the joint family properties were effected to his name.
But the plaintiffs and the defendants are in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties and the plaintiffs have acquired right, title or interest jointly.
But due to enlargement of joint family, some branches of the family are residing separately, but there is no partition and separate possession between the members of the family.

He has further deposed that after the demise of Achappa the defendants started acting adverse to the interest of joint family and as such, the plaintiffs did not want to continue in the joint family and hence, they approached the defendants to effect partition and initially though they agreed to effect partition later on postponed O.S. No.2353/2013 the same on one or the other pretext and thereafter, the defendants in collusion with each other and without consent or knowledge of the plaintiffs, partitioned all the schedule properties and got mutated the revenue records in their name under partition deed dated 17.02.2003 and
hence, the said partition deed which is executed without their consent or knowledge is not binding upon them.

Further the land bearing Sy. No.147/1 was acquired by K.I.A.D.B. and compensation amount is awarded and these plaintiffs are also entitled for share in the compensation amount and sought to decree the suit.

20. In support of his evidence P.W.1, he has relied upon Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 which are the RTCs,
revenue records pertaining to the suit schedule properties which shows they stand in the name of deceased Achappa from the year 1966-67 to 1975-76.
Ex.P.7 is the record of O.S. No.2353/2013 rights which shows that these properties are acquired by Achappa by virtue of inheritance and they are shown as ancestral properties.

Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.12 are the Encumbrance Certificate and Khata Extract which shows no Encumbrance Certificate is created over the suit property from 01.04.2004 to 03.03.2012 and Ex.P.13 is the disputed partition deed which shows the defendant No.1 and his mother Lakshmamma as first party and the defendant No.2 and his mother Rathnamma as second party have entered into partition pertaining to the suit schedule properties and they have divided the properties among themselves.
Ex.P.14 is the Memo of calculation submitted in Execution No.1185/2004 which shows it was filed for recovery of the award amount.
Ex.P.15 is the death certificate of deceased Narayanappa which shows he died on 29.07.1981 and the place of death is shown as Jeevanahalli, Bengaluru.

Relying on the place of death mentioned in this document, it is contended that O.S. No.2353/2013 the Narayanappa was residing at Bengaluru along with his brothers and as such there was no division of their joint family and they resided together.
Ex.P.16 is the Genealogical tree which is not in dispute and is discussed herein before.

21. During cross-examination of P.W.1 he denies the suggestion putforth that his father has sold his undivided  share in favour of Achappa under the sale deed dated 04.06.1952 and he was residing at Ajjavara Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk & District.

He has denied the suggestion putforth that Ramakrishnappa also sold his share under the registered Sale Deed 17.09.1962 and also pleads ignorance pertaining to the previous litigation that took place the defendant No.1 and his father Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
8 Achappa.

However, there is an unequivocal admission that a partition deed is entered into between the defendants No.1 and 2 and based on the partition O.S. No.2353/2013 deed khata is effected to their respective names and they are in possession and enjoyment of their respective shares.

So the evidence of P.W.1 shows, though he admits the partition between the defendants No.1 and 2, he has emphatically denied the execution of sale deed by his father in favour of father of defendant No.1 and he claims that the suit properties are their joint family properties.
So from the evidence of P.W.1, it shows he has consistently deposed about the existence of joint family status.
But admits that the defendant No.1 and 2 are in possession of their respective shares under the partition.

So the oral testimony of PW 1 coupled with the documents placed on record shows after the demise of propositus Muniyappa, the documents are transferred to the name of Achappa by virtue of inheritance and it is shown to be their ancestral properties.
So by this the plaintiff has discharged his initial burden of proving the joint status.
As stated earlier, the defendant No.1 has raised a specific defense as to the sale of undivided share in favor of Achappa, by the two brothers and as such the joint family is severed.
So now the onus shifts on the defendant to prove the legal necessity of Narayanappa to sell his undivided share in favor of Achappa.
It is settled legal proposition, that the term "legal necessity" has a very wide connotation.
It does not connote to an event or action that is imperative or indispensable, rather, it connotes to an event or action that is necessary for maintenance or management of joint family property.
As a matter of general principle, alienation by the karta shall bind the interest of all coparceners as he has discretion to ascertain whether a legal necessity and benefit of estate exists.

The alienation by the Manager or Karta of a joint family so as to bind the interest of coparceners is only available O.S. No.2353/2013 provided the alienation is either for legal necessity or for the benefit of the estates.

23. So in order to discharge the onus, the defendant No.1 got examined himself as D.W.1 and he has in his evidence deposed that the propositus of Muniyappa died prior to 1950 leaving behind his sons and his legal heirs and the father of second plaintiff Narayanappa transferred his undivided  share in the properties owned by the family in favour of his father Late.

Achappa under registered Sale Deed dated 04.06.1952 for valuable consideration and he got settled at Ajjavara Village, at Chikkaballapura Taluk & District and acquired immovable properties in the said village and neither the plaintiffs nor any other persons claiming under Narayanappa can make any claim over the schedule properties in view of execution of sale deed.

He has further deposed that on the same day his father O.S. No.2353/2013 Late. Achappa and his two brothers Ramakrishnappa and Munishamappa mortgaged the schedule properties in favour of one Mr. Fathe Chand Sait and after the demise of Munishamappa, Late. Achappa along with his mother Chowdamma and his brother Ramakrishnappa sold the suit schedule properties in favour of one Ramaiah S/o. Chatra Subbaiah under sale deed dated 23.05.1956 for the purpose of discharge of amount due under the mortgage deed.

Thereafter, Achappa and Ramakrishnappa repurchased the properties from Ramaiah under sale deed dated 11.07.1960 and subsequently, Ramakrishnappa also transferred his undivided share in favour of Late. Achappa under sale deed dated 17.09.1962 and thus Late.
Achappa continued in possession of these properties and he was the absolute owner thereof.

Further by virtue of the Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
9 decree passed in O.S. No.784/1980 and RFA. No.415/1987, the defendant No.1 was entitled for  O.S. No.2353/2013 share in the suit schedule properties.

During the pendency of the suit, Late.
Achappa executed a Will in favour of defendant No.2 without referring to the judgment passed and therefore, in order to put an end to the dispute, the defendant No.1 along with his mother Lakshmamma and defendant No.2 along with his mother Rathnamma entered into registered partition deed dated 17.12.2003.
By virtue of the said partition the defendant No.2 has affirmed the title of defendant No.1 and vice- versa,

Based on the partition deed khata is effected to the names of the parties and hence, the plaintiffs have no right over the schedule properties and the suit is filed to harass these defendants and sought for dismissal of suit.

24. In support of his evidence D.W.1, he has relied upon Ex.D.1 which is the certified copy of sale deed dated 11.07.1960 which shows one Ramaiah S/o.
O.S. No.2353/2013

Chatra Subbaiah sold the property in favour of Achappa and Ramakrishnappa and the terms of the sale deed shows that the vendor Ramaiah had purchased the schedule property on 23.05.1956 and the purchasers in the sale deed had entered into agreement with vendor on 23.05.1956 and as per agreement it was agreed to sell the property to the purchasers provided they paid a sum of Rs.3,000/- within 5 years and the purchasers expressed their willingness to pay Rs.3,000/- and hence, the property is reconveyed in favour of purchasers.

Ex.D.6 is the certified copy of the sale deed dated 04.06.1952 which shows Narayanappa has sold his  share in favour of Achappa in the family properties and so far as the reasons for sale of properties is concerned, it is stated that, he was at that point of time residing at Ajjavara Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk &
District and he had purchased some property in the said village and hence for the purpose of constructing a house, he has O.S. No.2353/2013 alienated his ancestral property for sale consideration amount of Rs.2,000/- and he had received Rs.500/- on 10.03.1952 and on the date of execution of the sale deed he has received Rs.1,500/- and has executed sale deed in respect of his share in favour of Achappa.

Ex.D.7 is the sale deed dated 23.05.1956 which shows much prior to the purchase of property from Ramaiah i.e. Ex.D.1. Achappa along with his mother Chowdamma and also Ramakrishnappa had sold the property in favour of Ramaiah and the recitals of the sale deed shows Narayanappa had released his rights in favour of rest of the members of the family and Muniyappa died 29 years ago and Achappa and Ramakrishnappa have sold the property in favour of Ramaiah.
It also recites that Narayanappa sold his right in favour of Achappa under a deed dated 04.06.1952 which is none other than the Ex.D.6 placed on record.

Likewise, the Ex.D.8 which is the sale deed dated 17.09.1962 which shows the other O.S. No.2353/2013 share holder Ramakrishnappa has also sold his  share in favour of Achappa for valuable consideration of Rs.1,000/-.
Ex . D.9
to Ex .D.24
which are the property tax paid receipts and
khata certificate shows the name of defendant No.1 is effected pertaining to the properties and he is paying tax to the concerned authorises.

So these documents relied upon by the defendant No.1 clearly shows Narayanappa and Ramakrishnappa have sold their undivided share in favour of defendant No.1 father Achappa and so far as necessity for the sale is concerned in Ex.D.6 it is clearly mentioned that the property is being sold by the father of the plaintiff No.2 for the purpose of legal and family necessity and for the benefit of the family.

During cross-examination of D.W.1 he says during the lifetime of his grand father Muniyappa partition is effected and all his sons started residing separately O.S. No.2353/2013 and in the partition, the property in Sy. No.160/1 measuring 1 acre 17 guntas and Sy. No.162 measuring 1 acre 12 guntas was allotted to the share of his father.

But though such a fact is stated in his cross-examination, there is no pleading as to the partition effected during the lifetime of his grand father in the written statement and this is contrary to the defense raised by the defendant No.1 in his written statement.
Hence this statement of D.W.1 in his cross-examination holds no significance.

D.W.1 pleads ignorance to the suggestion putforth that his father by misusing the trust of his uncle,
created the sale deed at Ex.D.6 and Ex.D.7.
D.W.1 admits that as per Ex.D.15 at the time of death Narayanappa is shown to be residing at Jeevanahalli, Bengaluru.

There is also admission of acquisition of land by KIADB and as to the award passed and also admits during the pendency of the suit in L.A.C. No.508/1980 Narayanappa died and his legal heirs were not brought on record.

So on analysis of the oral evidence of P.W.1 and D.W.1 coupled with the documents placed on record.

No doubt, the documents clearly speaks that all the revenue documents pertaining to the suit schedule properties were effected to the name of Achappa and the mode of acquisition is shows as ancestral.
There is no document forth coming to show there was partition among the four brothers either during the lifetime Muniyappa and father of his demise.

However, the sale deeds produced by the defendant No.1 shows that after the demise of Muniyappa it was Achappa who was managing the joint family affairs and he took care of the welfare of family as kartha of the joint family.
The sale deed which is at Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.7

shows that for the purpose of family necessities the Achappa and his brother Ramakrishnappa have sold the property in favour of one Ramaiah on 04.06.1952 and the sale deed which is marked as Ex.D.7 makes it clear that Narayanappa O.S. No.2353/2013 had already sold his right under the sale deed dated 04.06.1952 and as per Ex.D.1 the property is reconveyed in favour of Achappa and Ramakrishnappa and Ramakrishnappa in turn sold his undivided share in favour of Achappa on 11.07.1960.
However in view of the execution of the WILL by Achappa in favour of defendant No.2 they subsequently entered into partition deed which is now under challenge.

Thus on analysis of the entire evidence placed on record, it is evident from the sale deeds placed on record which is of the year 1950-60 that there was severance of joint status among the 3 brothers and the two brothers have sold their undivided share in favour of Achappa.

So, in the instant case as stated earlier it is established that the father of the plaintiff No.2 being manager of his family has alienated the property for the purpose of construction of house in the property acquired at Ajjavara village.
The defendant No.1 has established that the Narayanappa has alienated the property for the purpose of his family necessity.
The plaintiffs have not challenged the sale deed which is marked as Ex.D.6.
The father of the plaintiff No.2 also during his lifetime has not challenge the sale deed.
So by this it can be held that Narayanappa has admitted the sale of his share in favour of his brother and so during his life time he has not challenged the sale deed.
This establishes the severance of joint status among the plaintiffs and the defendants.

No doubt the place of death in death certificate Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
11 shows that Narayanppa died at Jeevanahalli Bangalore.

sentences.text: No doubt family members living in the same house are presumed to be joint living.
But it is rebuttal when it is proved by other evidence.
When the sale deed shows he was residing at Ajjavara, relying on an entry made in the death certificate, it cannot be held that they lived jointly.
The defendant No.1 has succeeded in O.S. No.2353/2013 establishing that the alienation was for family necessity and the sale would bind the plaintiffs.

Thus in view of the reasons assigned so far, this Court is of opinion that the plaintiffs failed to prove that the suit schedule properties are ancestral joint family properties of plaintiffs and defendants and they are in joint possession and enjoyment of the same and that the Partition Deed dated 17.02.2003 is not binding on them.
Hence, the plaintiffs are not entitled for the relief of partition as claimed.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to answer issues No.1 to 3 and 5 in the Negative.
28. ISSUE NO.4 ::
The present suit was initially filed for the relief of partition and separate possession on 22.03.2013.

However, during the pendency of the suit by way of amendment on 28.10.2014 the plaintiffs have sought for declaration that the registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003 effected between defendants No.1 and O.S. No.2353/2013 2 is not binding on the plaintiffs.

The defendant No.1 has raised a specific contention that the plaintiffs have deliberately suppressed the registered transactions and judicial proceedings in respect of the properties over last 60 to 70 years and the members of this defendant family is in possession and enjoyment of the properties allotted under final decree proceedings and hence, there is no cause of action to file the suit and the suit is hopelessly barred by law of limitation.
No doubt, there is no specific period of limitation prescribed to file the suit suit for partition and the suit for partition can be filed by coparceners of the property at any time.
However, the parties have challenged registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003.
So as per Article 110 of Limitation Act, the plaintiffs has file the suit within 12 years from the date when the exclusion becomes known to the plaintiffs.

So in the instant case,
the parties are challenging the partition deed dated 17.02.2003 and so the suit is filed O.S.
No.2353/2013 well within period of 12 years from the date of execution of partition deed and hence,
the suit is within law of limitation and the contention raised by the defendant No.1 that the suit is barred by law of limitation holds no significance.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to answer the aforesaid issue No.4 in the Negative.
29. ISSUE NO.6 ::

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following;
 ORDER  The suit of the plaintiffs is  dismissed.
Both parties shall bear the cost of  the suit.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The present suit is one for partition and separate possession of plaintiffs  share together in the suit schedule properties and for declaration that the registered partition deed dated 17.02.2003 is not binding upon the plaintiffs.
In the instant case, the relationship between the parties is not in dispute.
One Muniyappa and his wife Chowdamma are the original propositus of the family of the plaintiffs and the defendants and he had O.S. No.2353/2013 4 sons by name Achappa,
Narayanappa, Ramakrishnappa and Munishamappa.
According to the plaintiffs, the suit schedule properties are the ancestral and joint family properties and after the demise of Muniyappa,
the Achappa being the eldest member of the family looked after the family affairs as khartha of the joint family and as such, the suit schedule properties stood in his name.
the other son Ramakrishnappa also transferred his undivided share in favour of Achappa and hence,
there exists no joint family among the family members and the defendants No.1 and 2 by entering into partition deed have partitioned the property which belonged to Achappa and hence, the plaintiffs are not entitled for any share.
However, Achappa contested the suit and raised a defense that the suit schedule properties are the joint family properties of himself and his other two brothers Narayanappa and Ramakrishnappa and there was no partition among them and any documents executed by their brothers were O.S. No.2353/2013 nominal and were not intended to be acted upon and there was no income from any of these properties and the suit properties were his self acquisitions acquired out of his separate income and had sought for dismissal of suit.
However, the Court held that the Achappa failed to prove his Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
6 separate income to purchase the share of his brothers in the schedule items and therefore, the suit schedule lands were considered to be ancestral and joint family properties of the plaintiff and defendant No.1 therein and hence, the suit was decreed and the defendant No.1 herein was held entitled for  share in the suit schedule items No.1 to 5 and he was also held entitled for compensation amount pertaining to the acquisition of item No.4 of the schedule land.
So the Hon'ble High Court has held that the suit properties therein where the ancestral and joint family properties constituted by the defendant No.1 and his father Achappa.
It is well settled proposition of law that there is always presumption as to the existence of joint family status between the parties.
In Hindu law, a joint family is presumed to exist among Hindu coparceners and they are presumed to be members of a pint family.
However the presumption can be rebutted by showing that the family has been severed.
But in the instant case, since the plaintiffs are challenging the partition deed, the initial burden is upon them to prove the existence of joint Manjula vs Balakrishna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96586430/
So now the onus shifts on the defendant to prove the legal necessity of Narayanappa to sell his undivided share in favor of Achappa.
It is settled legal proposition, that the term "legal necessity" has a very wide connotation.
It does not connote to an event or action that is imperative or indispensable, rather, it connotes to an event or action that is necessary for maintenance or management of joint family property.
As a matter of general principle, alienation by the karta shall bind the interest of all coparceners as he has discretion to ascertain whether a legal necessity and benefit of estate exists.
The alienation by the Manager or Karta of a joint family so as to bind the interest of coparceners is only available O.S. No.2353/2013 provided the alienation is either for legal necessity or for the benefit of the estates.
During the pendency of the suit, Late.
Achappa executed a Will in favour of defendant No.2 without referring to the judgment passed and therefore, in order to put an end to the dispute, the defendant No.1 along with his mother Lakshmamma and defendant No.2 along with his mother Rathnamma entered into registered partition deed dated 17.12.2003.
Thus on analysis of the entire evidence placed on record, it is evident from the sale deeds placed on record which is of the year 1950-60 that there was severance of joint status among the 3 brothers and the two brothers have sold their undivided share in favour of Achappa.
When the sale deed shows he was residing at Ajjavara, relying on an entry made in the death certificate, it cannot be held that they lived jointly.
The defendant No.1 has succeeded in O.S. No.2353/2013 establishing that the alienation was for family necessity and the sale would bind the plaintiffs.

So as per Article 110 of Limitation Act, the plaintiffs has file the suit within 12 years from the date when the exclusion becomes known to the plaintiffs.
